subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should config-write validation for `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` warn on unknown entries, fail closed, or remain audit-only for custom/plugin command compatibility?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing a gateway security-control write path can affect custom or plugin command IDs and operator workflows, so automation should not choose the security policy unilaterally.

options.title: Warn on unknown entries
options.body: Reuse the audit command catalog and suggestions during `openclaw config set/patch`, but still persist custom or plugin command IDs.

options.title: Fail closed on unknown entries
options.body: Reject unknown denylist entries during config writes and require an explicit escape hatch or catalog registration story for custom commands.

options.title: Keep audit-only
options.body: Leave config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to diagnose ineffective entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn on unknown entries
recommendation.body: Reuse the audit command catalog and suggestions during `openclaw config set/patch`, but still persist custom or plugin command IDs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history across security audit hardening, node command catalog behavior, and split audit tests around this surface.
